analysis.investment_thesis: Devyani is a real business with strong brand licenses (KFC, Pizza Hut) and 19% revenue CAGR, but the market at 127x forward P/E and 28x EV/EBITDA is pricing in flawless execution of a turnaround that hasn't happened in nine years. You are being asked to pay a premium for profits that have consistently failed to materialize at the net level.
key_strengths: Brand portfolio durability — KFC/Pizza Hut franchise rights provide structural volume and pricing power in India's growing QSR market
Operating cash flow consistently positive (5/5 years, growing from INR 301 Cr in FY20 to INR 900 Cr in FY25) — the business does generate cash before debt service
Promoter holding of 61.37% with RJ Corp as parent provides operational continuity and reputational incentive to not destroy the franchise
key_risks: Chronic net losses — profitable in only 2 of last 9 years; FY25 net loss of INR 7 Cr despite INR 4,951 Cr revenue shows the unit economics are structurally impaired at the bottom line

Debt load is dangerously high: INR 3,188 Cr total debt vs INR 853 Cr EBITDA = 3.74x Debt/EBITDA (above 3.0x threshold), with finance costs of INR 267 Cr growing at 22.5% CAGR — a rate hike cycle or revenue slowdown creates solvency stress
FCF yield of only 3.1% (INR 418 Cr FCF / INR 13,279 Cr market cap) — far below the 6-8% minimum required for an acceptable risk/reward; you are getting paid almost nothing to own this risk
red_flags: 127x forward P/E on a company that earned negative net profit in FY24 AND FY25 — the 'forward' in that P/E is purely aspirational
Finance costs (INR 267 Cr) consume 31% of EBITDA (INR 853 Cr) — there is no margin for operational missteps before interest coverage deteriorates dangerously

Borrowings nearly tripled from INR 1,254 Cr (FY22) to INR 3,343 Cr (FY25), funded partly by the IPO; capital is being deployed aggressively while returns on capital (ROCE 6.42%) sit below any reasonable cost of capital
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking demands we ask not "is Devyani a good QSR operator?" but "what does INR 108 per share already assume?" At EV/EBITDA of 28x and 127x forward P/E, the market has priced in a near-perfect trajectory: sustained 20%+ revenue growth, meaningful margin expansion, and a dramatic net profit inflection — all simultaneously. The historical record refutes this: the company has posted net losses in seven of the last nine years, and even the brief profit window in FY22-FY23 evaporated immediately (FY24: -10 Cr, FY25: -7 Cr). Finance costs at INR 267 Cr and growing at 22.5% CAGR are the silent killer here — every rupee of EBITDA improvement is being partly offset by the rising cost of the debt machine funding expansion. ROCE of 6.42% against a cost of debt that must exceed 8% means the business is destroying value on an incremental basis at the current leverage level.

The one genuinely positive data point is operating cash flow — INR 900 Cr in FY25, FCF of INR 418 Cr — which demonstrates the franchise economics do work at the store level. But a 3.1% FCF yield offers no margin of safety. In a stress scenario (consumer slowdown, commodity cost spike, or interest rate reversion), debt/EBITDA already at 3.74x could spike to 5x+ quickly, threatening refinancing and potentially equity dilution. Howard Marks' framework is unambiguous here: the asymmetry is terrible — limited upside from a stock already pricing perfection, and severe downside if growth slows or rates rise. The current price compensates you for none of the risk you are accepting.
